items.q: You open a terminal and type `python3 --version`. What does this tell you?
options: Whether the Python interpreter is installed and which version it is
The version of your operating system

explain.right: Python is both a language and the interpreter program that runs it; `--version` confirms that program is installed and reports its 3.x version.
explain.wrong: It isn't about the web, hardware speed, or the OS version; it only reports the Python interpreter.

items.q: What is the REPL (the `>>>` prompt you get by running `python3` with no file)?
options: A permanent program that saves all your code automatically
The only way to run Python
A place to type one line at a time and see its result instantly, which forgets everything when closed

explain.right: REPL = Read-Evaluate-Print-Loop: it runs one line immediately and shows the result, but keeps nothing after you close it.
explain.wrong: It saves nothing, isn't the only way to run Python (files are), and isn't a website.

items.q: You run `python3 todo.py`. In what order does Python execute the lines in the file?
options: Only the lines that contain print()
Strictly top to bottom, one line after another

explain.right: The interpreter reads and runs a script top to bottom in order; using something before it's defined fails because that line hasn't run yet.
explain.wrong: Execution isn't random, reversed, or limited to print lines — every line runs, in order.

items.q: In the REPL, typing `2 + 2` and pressing Enter shows `4`. You put the single line `2 + 2` in a file and run it. What appears?
options: Nothing — a script doesn't auto-print values; you'd need print(2 + 2)

explain.right: The REPL auto-prints the value of each line; a script only outputs what you explicitly print, so a bare `2 + 2` shows nothing.
explain.wrong: It isn't an error and doesn't echo the text; the difference is that files don't auto-print like the REPL does.

items.q: In one or two sentences, explain the difference between the REPL and running a `.py` file.
rubric: REPL runs one line at a time and shows the result immediately
REPL forgets everything when closed; a file is saved and reusable
A file runs top to bottom and only prints what you tell it to

explain.right: Good answers note the REPL is interactive and throwaway while a file is saved, runs in order, and prints only on request.
explain.wrong: A weak answer says only 'one is typing and one is a file' without the saved / auto-print / order distinctions.
